Notes

狙击你的虚荣心

狙击 is a sniper attack or targeted strike. The target here is explicitly 虚荣心, vanity, so the English keeps the act of aiming without inventing a physical victim.

  • Genius community transcript
侥幸

侥幸 especially suggests obtaining a good outcome or escaping trouble by chance. The following “no escape” makes that shade stronger than generic good fortune. Later, the speaker says he has kept working and fighting; the song grants others no lucky exit while claiming his own position through effort.

  • Lyric text
棉花糖泡泡糖

HARIBO is the German confectionery company known for fruit gummies; its name combines Hans Riegel and Bonn. The title prepares a sweet, brightly packaged association, while the verse speaks about vanity, capture, and fate. The named sweets give that contrast a physical texture, without identifying a particular HARIBO product.

  • HARIBO: company history
  • Lyric text
香精色素

After cotton candy and bubble gum, the lyric breaks sweets down into flavorings and colors piled together. The text supplies this manufactured-sweetness image but does not explicitly explain what it stands for.

  • Genius community transcript
命

命 can refer to life, a life span, or fate. In this line, following the insistence that there is no escape, “fate” preserves the sense of something assigned or unavoidable.

  • Genius community transcript
